Distributed event streaming platform
Built to store, process, and transport streams of events

blocks.html: Event
An event is a fact that happened
blocks.text: An event is a fact that happened

blocks.html: It represents something that already occurred
blocks.text: It represents something that already occurred

blocks.html: It is immutable (cannot be changed)
Examples:
“User registered”
“Order placed”
“Payment failed”
Event vs normal data (important)
Normal data:
“User name is Lal”
Event:
“User name was set to Lal at 10:05”
blocks.text: “User name was set to Lal at 10:05”

blocks.html: Difference:
Event includes action + time
Why events are never changed
You cannot change the past
If something changes:
A new event is created
Example:
Event 1: “Order created”
Event 2: “Order cancelled”
What Kafka stores
Kafka stores events only
Each event is:
Appended
Never updated
Never edited
Kafka behaves like:
A notebook
You only append lines (events)
You never erase immediately
Anyone can read from any line

user-signups
orders
payments

Never modified

Order is preserved
Replay is possible
Concurrency is safe
History is trustworthy

A topic can have one partition.
